rename.from: "no-unused-vars" report only the last function parameter
rename.to: "no-unused-vars" reports only the last function parameter

body:
Thanks for the issue report. I believe this rule is behaving as intended. It only warns on the last function parameter because you might have to define the previous parameters to be able to access it in the function body (so the last parameter defined should always be used when this rule is enabled). 

It looks to me like `argsIgnorePattern` is also working as intended, as it then ignores any cases that match the regex (which, in your example, `_next` does). Does that make sense?

@kaicataldo I'm not sure I agree. In the first example, next is unused, so req and res should not be "protected" by the (non-)use of next. In the second example, ignoring a parameter isn't the same as using it (or at least shouldn't be), so I wouldn't want req and res to be passed over in that case either.

Both of those seem like potential bugs to me, especially the second.

Thank you for this issue.

This happens by the other option, [`args`](http://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-unused-vars#args).
The `args` option of `no-unused-vars` rule is `"after-used"` by default. This option will warn only the last argument. You can use another option `"all"`.

I'm interested in a change of the behavior.
It sounds good to me if `"after-used"` option warns the last parameter which isn't ignored.
By the way, @julienw might be interested in [no-use-ignored-vars](https://github.com/mysticatea/eslint-plugin/blob/master/docs/rules/no-use-ignored-vars.md) rule of my plugin. :smiley:
Labeled as `enhancement`, but feel free to change it to `bug` if that seems more apt.

Yeah, I think this is a bug since we can overlook unused variables.
I'm working on this.
